tagline: To the gold camps by stage road and ore-train grade.
intro: From Cañon City the Shelf Road heads north up Fourmile Canyon past Garden Park. It was built in 1892 as a toll road for stagecoaches and wagons, and in one stretch it clings to the canyon wall 200 feet above the stream. It comes out at Cripple Creek and Victor, where gold is still mined, and the way back down is Phantom Canyon, on the bed of an old ore railroad.
That railroad climbed 4,550 feet in 30 miles. It took on a helper engine at Cramer and water at Adelaide. A paved third leg, High Park Road, crosses open cattle range with Pikes Peak in view.

moments.title: Garden Park
moments.text: A valley named for the vegetables it grew for Cripple Creek miners, where Marsh and Cope made finds in the Bone Wars. One of its Stegosaurus is at the National Museum of Natural History.

moments.title: Victor
moments.text: In 1894 the Woods brothers hit gold while digging a building foundation in town, and that was the start of the Gold Coin Mine. Jack Dempsey worked as a mucker in the Portland.

moments.title: Phantom Canyon
moments.text: The gravel road follows Eight Mile Creek on the old Florence and Cripple Creek grade, through two tunnels cut in granite that never needed timber and across the 1897 Steel Bridge.

practical: Phantom Canyon and Shelf Road are narrow and rugged in places. No vehicles over 25 feet long on Phantom Canyon Road, and four-wheel drive is recommended on the upper Shelf Road.
